properties.decision:
DECIDED on Anthony's word, 2026-08-24, choosing between three costed options: "An edge: a claim". A record that did the work says so, with `INVALIDATES` (`* -> *`, carrying `note` and `at`), rather than a detector inferring staleness from dates.

WHAT THE ALTERNATIVE WAS AND WHY IT LOST — and it lost on a MEASUREMENT, not on taste. The cheaper option was a computed bucket: `loop_status.verifications.stale`, a failing check whose verified nodes changed since its last run. It needs no discipline, which is the strongest argument any option here had. It is also unbuildable honestly: the inference has to order a change against `last_run_at`, and of 439 hand-written ChangeEvents only 37 (8%) carried a date, against 84% of the 192 written by the reconcile paths. The difference was not care — `add_change_event` had no `detected_at` parameter, so the ordinary path could not date anything. A bucket built on that would have over- or under-reported and been unable to say which.

⭐ THE EDGE IS GENERAL AND THAT IS THE POINT. dev_storyflow proposed `INVALIDATES_RUN` for Constraint -> Verification. The same missing relation was measured independently on this project and on Anthony's other machine, both times on a TemporalFact rather than a Verification — see `dec:idea-how-does-the-graph-learn-what-a-session-invalidated`, whose option C asked for "an edge from a ChangeEvent to the finding it ANSWERS". Two projects, three sightings, two node types, one relation. So the `_RUN` suffix came off and both endpoints stayed open.

⭐⭐ IT CLAIMS THE RESULT IS STALE AND NOTHING MORE, which is why it is not called `RESOLVES` — the first name tried. A repair does not make a check pass; it makes the last RESULT untrustworthy, and only a re-run can say what is true now. `RESOLVES` would have reflow2 asserting an outcome nobody measured, which is `dec:non-goal-reflow2-does-not-judge-whether-a-check-is-meaningful` one step along. Three consequences follow and all three are load-bearing: the edge never touches the target's `status`; the check is NOT dropped from `loop_status.verifications.attention`, because silencing it would swap one wrong reading for another and would be the truncation `parks` was careful not to become; and `rerun_owed` is THREE-VALUED, with null meaning one side is undated and nobody can say — never collapsed to false.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE. The computed bucket is deferred, not refused: `add_change_event` now takes `detected_at`, so the ordering it needs becomes possible as dates accumulate. Whether to build it then is open, and the parent brainstorm's options A, B and E are untouched.
properties.name: A finding is closed by a CLAIM, not by an inferred staleness
properties.rationale:
Prompted by dev_storyflow's 2026-08-23 report, which cost a real user a real instruction: a session read a `failing` check dated that same day and reported its two defects as the live state of the system, when both had been repaired hours earlier and written up on two Constraint nodes. `describe_schema(from: Constraint, to: Verification)` returned ZERO exact matches; the reporter drew `CONTRADICTS` with `alignment: opposing` and called it "obviously a stand-in".

The prior decision on this ground was READ BEFORE DECIDING AND DOES NOT COVER THIS CASE. `dec:verification-freshness-not-a-gap` (accepted, Anthony, 2026-07-26) ruled that a check older than its code is a freshness FACT rather than a gap, because it is a STANDING PROPERTY that "would fire on every legitimate refactor as readily as on a real hole". This is a different question: a repair landing against a FAILING check is an EVENT, it fires once, and it fires only where there is both a failure and a repair. So this settles new ground rather than reversing a settled decision — and it honours that decision's reasoning by making the result a REPORT beside the check rather than a new nag.
